title: With Cal Raleigh’s three-home run night, the Mariners bounce back
content:
One day after the drubbing of the season, it was the Seattle Mariners doing the trouncing. More specifically, it was Cal Raleigh, who had the best game of his year in Seattle’s 9-2 win over the Philadelphia Phillies. So much so that the Mariners allegedly ran out of fireworks after Raleigh bashed three home runs, two of which came off of Zack Wheeler.

Just like that, the Mariners catcher, marred in a career-worst season, improved upon nearly every metric after going 3-for-3 with four RBIs and a walk. The runner-up to last year’s American League MVP award improved his season-long wRC+ to 83 (up from 73) and his slash line went from .159/.275/.304 (.579 OPS) to .167/.282/.336 (.618 OPS).

It was the first three-homer game of Raleigh’s career, and also the first time a player homered three times at Seattle’s T-Mobile Park. Not since Edgar Martínez in 1999 had a Mariner gone deep three times in a single home game.

“I had never done that before at any level, so hard to fathom,” Raleigh said. “It was a fun night.”

Monday marked Raleigh’s 22nd multi-homer game in a Seattle uniform, moving him into a tie with Martínez and Jay Buhner for second-most in Mariners franchise history, per MLB.com’s Sarah Langs. At the top is Ken Griffey Jr., with 44.

The last Seattle catcher to go deep three times in a game? None other than Raleigh’s skipper, Dan Wilson, who did so in 1996.

For Raleigh, Monday’s contest represented another step in the right direction. After a 9.1 fWAR season in 2025, Raleigh has disappointed, posting career lows in multiple offensive categories.

“We’re not playing well, that starts with me — I’m awful,” Raleigh told reporters in early August. “So it is what it is. I’ve got to find a way to be better and to help bring the guys along, and we’ve just got to play better.”

Since then, Raleigh has largely turned it around. He’s posted a .797 OPS in August to go with six home runs.

Monday’s win could not have come at more opportune time for Seattle, which remains in the playoff race despite a losing record (63-69). The Mariners ended Monday three games behind the Texas Rangers for the American League West lead and three games out of the AL’s third and final wild-card spot.

To get there, Seattle will have to weather one of the toughest remaining parts of its schedule; two more games against the Phillies, followed by three games each against the Toronto Blue Jays and Boston Red Sox.

“We know we’re a good team and we know we got a lot of good opponents coming up,” Raleigh said. “It’s just about belief and hope and I think bringing that every day no matter what happens is a strong powerful thing to have in the clubhouse. Right now, I think that’s what the guys are doing.”
